clauses.quote: Authors and reviewers MUST prefer the built-in expression AST (Section 4) over the closed function registry (Section 9). A `{"op": "fn", ...}` node is justified **only** when the desired primitive cannot be written as a finite closed-form composition of the AST ops in §4.2 — typically because it requires non-AST ingredients (calendar arithmetic, polygon clipping). Anything expressible in finite closed form (powers, polynomials, transcendentals, conditionals, piecewise, clip/clamp) belongs in the AST. Reviewers MUST reject `fn` nodes whose body can be written using existing AST ops
clauses.note: Authoring and review policy for adding registry functions; not a property of document semantics.

clauses.quote: bindings MUST reject any `fn` node whose `name` is not in the spec-defined set for the file's declared `esm` version
clauses.note: A document is rejected at load iff some fn node names a function absent from the registry for its declared esm version.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST normalize it away **at load**, so the typed document never holds a block with nothing set and the block does not survive `parse → emit`.
clauses.note: load maps `solver: {}` to an absent solver block, so emit(load d) carries no solver key when the block was empty.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST NOT read absence as an assertion about the system.
clauses.note: The loaded representation distinguishes an absent stiffness (or absent block) from any declared value, e.g. absent ≠ "low".

clauses.quote: A binding MUST run it at *every* entry point that hands a document to an integrator
clauses.note: The tolerances an integrator receives are call-site argument, else solver.abstol/reltol, else binding default, at every integration entry point (solve and init).

clauses.quote: a binding MUST be able to tell "the caller named no tolerance" apart from "the caller passed the binding default"
clauses.note: Constrains the signature of a binding's entry points (optional vs defaulted arguments), not format semantics.

clauses.quote: `external` MUST be a string of length at least 1 (a schema rule), and MUST NOT contain `${`, which is refused at load with `solver_external_unresolved` (§2.2.6).
clauses.note: solver.external is accepted only as a non-empty string; one containing `${` is rejected at load with solver_external_unresolved.

clauses.quote: `time_span` MUST carry both `start` and `end`, each a number or an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp (schema rules), and `end` MUST be after `start`, which is refused at load with `solver_time_span_invalid` (§2.2.7).
clauses.note: A time_span without both bounds of the admitted forms is a schema error; one whose converted end ≤ start is rejected with solver_time_span_invalid.

clauses.quote: Presence of `solver` MUST NOT alter equations, variable classification, namespacing, or the flattened system.
clauses.note: flatten(d) = flatten(d with any solver block), and classification is independent of solver.

clauses.quote: A document declaring `esm` below `1.1.0` and carrying a `solver` block MUST be rejected with `solver_version_too_old`.
clauses.note: A document with esm < 1.1.0 and a solver block is rejected with solver_version_too_old.

clauses.quote: A document declaring `esm` below `1.3.0` whose `solver` block carries `external` MUST be rejected with `solver_external_version_too_old`, before schema validation, at pointer `/solver/external`; one whose `solver` block carries `time_span` MUST be rejected with `solver_time_span_version_too_old`, before schema validation, at pointer `/solver/time_span`.
clauses.note: esm < 1.3.0 with solver.external (resp. time_span) yields exactly (solver_external_version_too_old, /solver/external) (resp. the time_span code and pointer), taking precedence over schema errors.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST NOT open, read, fetch or validate the document `external` names.
clauses.note: File/network access policy; the model performs no I/O.

clauses.quote: The message MUST name `/solver/external` and quote the string exactly as authored, between plain double quotes with nothing escaped.
clauses.note: The solver_external_unresolved message contains the pointer /solver/external and the authored string verbatim between double quotes.
clauses.concern: This pins diagnostic prose, while §4.9.6 says the prose is 'as everywhere else, not pinned across bindings'; and 'nothing escaped' makes the message ambiguous when the authored string itself contains a double quote or newline.

clauses.quote: It MUST NOT fail because of `external`, and it MUST NOT change its choice of integrator because `external` is present.
clauses.note: A binding's own solve/init behave identically on d and on d with solver.external added.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST NOT route a timestamp through a host date library whose range, leap-second or time-zone handling it does not control.
clauses.note: A timestamp bound converts to the binary64 value (W − W₀) + (f − f₀) defined by the proleptic Gregorian calendar, for every pattern-valid timestamp and origin.

clauses.quote: binding that honours it MUST let an explicit interval at the call site override it, with the resolution order of §2.2.2
clauses.note: The interval used for integration is the call-site interval (both bounds) if given, else the document's converted time_span, else none.

clauses.quote: core tooling MUST NOT assign meaning to anything inside it, MUST NOT validate or transform it, and MUST preserve it across `parse → emit` like any other metadata field.
clauses.note: For any JSON object x, metadata.x_esd = x survives emit(load d) unchanged and no verdict depends on its contents.

clauses.quote: That surface is normative for those APIs: `parse_expression` is the inverse of `to_ascii`, and all five bindings MUST agree on the reading of any given text.
clauses.note: parse_expression is a function of the text, and parse_expression(to_ascii e) = e for every expression e (up to the stated normalizations).
clauses.concern: 'parse_expression is the inverse of to_ascii' cannot hold for all trees: §4.1.1 itself says a parser flattens `a + (b + c)` into one n-ary `+` (so a nested `+` tree does not round-trip), and a `-` before a numeric literal is read as part of the literal (so a unary-minus node on a literal does not round-trip); the class of trees on which it is an inverse is not stated.

clauses.quote: Because a unary-minus operand extends only to the next `+` or binary `-`, a printer MUST parenthesize a negated sum or difference
clauses.note: to_ascii of a unary minus over a + or binary - node parenthesizes the operand, so the text re-parses to the same tree.

clauses.quote: because every level groups to the LEFT, a printer MUST parenthesize a right operand at the same level unless it is the same associative operator
clauses.note: to_ascii parenthesizes a right operand of equal precedence unless it is the same associative n-ary operator, so parse(to_ascii e) = e.
clauses.concern: 'every level groups to the LEFT' contradicts the precedence table, where level 7 `^` is right-associative and level 6 `not` is prefix; for `^` the rule as written parenthesizes the wrong side (a right `^` operand needs none, a left one does).

clauses.quote: A rewrite-target op has **no** evaluator; it MUST be eliminated by a rewrite rule (§9.6) before evaluation.
clauses.note: Evaluation/compilation of a document in which any open-tier op survives the rewrite fixpoint is rejected with unlowered_operator; loading is not.

clauses.quote: **A `D` the resolution cannot answer MUST be refused (normative).** Resolution answers nothing for an operand outside the table above — an operator with no rule there (`^`, an elementary function, a reduction, a nested `D`), or a name that carries neither equation and is not time-invariant — and it answers nothing for a **cyclic** chain, which it MUST detect and stop rather than expand without end (`D(x)/dt ~ k · D(x, t)`; an observed whose definition reaches its own derivative). In each case the node remains as authored and is a rewrite-target: an implementation MUST NOT invent a value for it
clauses.note: RHS total-derivative resolution is a terminating partial function defined by the table; on any operand outside it or on a cycle it leaves the D node unchanged (never 0), and the build rejects it with unlowered_operator.

clauses.quote: `args` MUST have exactly one entry. It is evaluable-core and is consumed by system assembly
clauses.note: A D node with wrt "t" or no wrt and an arg count other than one is rejected at load.
clauses.concern: The expected diagnostic is binding-dependent (a schema maxItems error, or operator_arity in a binding that also checks arity), so the clause does not fix one verdict code to pin.

clauses.quote: it MUST NOT report a trailing operand as an arity defect, and MUST NOT let one participate in, or invalidate, the derivative's dimension.
clauses.note: For a spatial D, the dimensional result and findings of D(f, aux…) equal those of D(f): trailing operands never affect the check.

clauses.quote: the format assigns no per-position role and a binding MUST NOT infer one
clauses.note: The meaning of args[1..] of a spatial D is fixed only by the matching rule: lowering depends on them solely through pattern binding.

clauses.quote: a checker MUST report their dimension as `unknown` and skip the enclosing check (§4.8.4), never inventing a coordinate-divided dimension
clauses.note: grad/div/laplacian/integral and every other open-tier op have undeterminable dimension, so the enclosing check is skipped.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST NOT single these names out
clauses.note: Matching, lowering and checking treat grad/div/laplacian/curl/integral exactly as any other open-tier op name (renaming invariance).

clauses.quote: Conforming bindings MUST reject `min`/`max` nodes with fewer than two arguments.
clauses.note: A min/max node with fewer than two arguments is rejected at load.

clauses.quote: A language's native min/max that drops NaN (Rust's `f64::max`, C's `fmax`, Python's built-in `max` in one argument order) MUST NOT be used as is.
clauses.note: min/max (and the max/min faq reduction) return NaN when any argument is NaN, in every argument position (ruling 2026-10-26).

clauses.quote: reviewers MUST reject `fn` nodes that only re-implement these in disguise
clauses.note: Review policy for registry additions; not a property of document semantics.

clauses.quote: `output` selects which output (integer index or named entry) to return. `args` MUST be empty.
clauses.note: A table_lookup node with non-empty args is rejected at load.

clauses.quote: `value` is any JSON value (number, integer, or nested array of numbers/integers); `args` MUST be empty `[]`.
clauses.note: A const node with non-empty args is rejected at load.

clauses.quote: `fn` MUST name a scalar operator, applied at an arity that operator admits, else `invalid_broadcast_fn`.
clauses.note: A broadcast node whose fn is not a pointwise scalar op, or is applied at an inadmissible arity, is rejected with invalid_broadcast_fn.

clauses.quote: A loader MUST accept it, MUST normalize the node to `faq` at the wire boundary — ahead of the version gates and schema validation, so that nothing downstream of the loader, `emit` included, ever sees the alias — and MUST report the warning diagnostic `deprecated_op_alias` once per document per alias.
clauses.note: load rewrites every `aggregate` node to `faq` (raising the declared esm to ≥ 1.1.0) and emits one deprecated_op_alias warning; emit never writes `aggregate`.
clauses.concern: It says normalization runs 'ahead of the version gates', but the next paragraph says the faq_version_too_old gate 'reads the authored form, before normalization' — the order is stated both ways; and 'once per document' is ambiguous when one load touches several documents (root, ref-loaded children, libraries), each of which is normalized.

clauses.quote: every column a `skolem` key, `distinct` producer or arg-witness body reads MUST be build-time data. A **constant factor** is any of: an array supplied to the build (a loader- or caller-provided factor), a shaped parameter carrying inline data (§6.3), or an **unknown whose defining equation's right-hand side is an array `const` node** (`x ~ const([…])`). The last is build-time data exactly as the first two are, so a binding MUST accept it as a key column.
clauses.note: A value-invention key column is admitted iff it is a constant factor (including x ~ const([…])); otherwise derived_index_set_unmaterialized or relational_node_in_continuous.

clauses.quote: MUST be rejected by `validate()` with `ragged_values_not_gathered` (§9.6.6)
clauses.note: validate rejects a non-value-invention faq ranging over a declared ragged set whose expr/filter never reads that set's values array (template references and injected sets excepted).

clauses.quote: binding MUST NOT introduce one under a private op name. The `integral` op (§4.2) is *not* the discrete cumulative form
clauses.note: Constrains a binding's op vocabulary; the format's closed evaluable core already excludes such an op.

clauses.quote: An evaluator that does not keep a running accumulator — a per-cell triangular fold, say — MUST still fold each cell's window in the variant's direction, so it reaches the same bits.
clauses.note: Each output cell of a forward (reverse) scan equals the left fold of its window in increasing (decreasing) contracted-index order, bitwise.

clauses.quote: the format ships no separate `scan` / `fold` / `recur` operator and a binding MUST NOT introduce one under a private op name
clauses.note: Constrains a binding's op vocabulary; the closed evaluable core already excludes such an op.

clauses.quote: a binding MUST reject a self-read it cannot justify rather than guessing at one
clauses.note: Every causal self-read is either admitted by the lag rules or the document is rejected with a recurrence_* code; no self-read is silently reinterpreted.

clauses.quote: The proof obligation is therefore split, and the split is normative. The **coefficient** of the frame symbol MUST be provably 1
clauses.note: A self-read index argument that is not affine in its frame symbol with coefficient 1 is rejected with recurrence_not_wellfounded.
clauses.concern: 'Provably 1' names no decision procedure: whether forms such as `(k+k)-k`, `1*k`, or `p*k` with a parameter p = 1 count as coefficient 1 is unspecified, so validators of different strength can reach different verdicts — the validator/evaluator divergence the following paragraph says is never defensible.

clauses.quote: need NOT be provable, and a checker MUST NOT reject a lag merely because it could not bound it
clauses.note: A self-read with coefficient 1 whose lag bounds are unknown or straddle zero is admitted; only provably non-positive lag is rejected.

clauses.quote: A recurrence definition MUST NOT be evaluated through any whole-array, vectorized, fused, tiled, kernel-merged or otherwise reordered path.
clauses.note: The value of a recurrence equals the ordered sweep (recurrence axis outermost ascending, each cell published before the next), bitwise.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST evaluate a recurrence identically on **every route it has** for materializing an observed
clauses.note: Per-step and build-time materialization of a recurrence observed produce identical bits.

clauses.quote: MUST do so with one shared implementation of the sweep rather than one per route
clauses.note: Code-structure requirement on a binding.

clauses.quote: A self-read that is not a well-founded causal read is a structural error, not a boundary case, and every binding MUST reject it
clauses.note: Each situation in the Rejections table yields exactly its listed code (recurrence_not_wellfounded or recurrence_unsupported_form).

clauses.quote: A binding that has to exempt the self-edge from an existing cycle check MUST gate that exemption on the equation being a **candidate**
clauses.note: An ill-founded self-read in an array-shaped candidate yields a recurrence_* code, never observed_cycle.

clauses.quote: A pair with `stop < start − 1` is **inverted** and MUST be rejected at load time with `makearray_region_inverted` (§9.6.6)
clauses.note: After metaparameter folding, a makearray bound pair with stop < start − 1 is rejected with makearray_region_inverted; stop = start − 1 is an empty region.

clauses.quote: A one-operand `broadcast` MUST NOT be treated as the identity on its operand
clauses.note: broadcast(fn, [x]) equals fn applied unarily to each element of x.

clauses.quote: Bindings **MUST emit an `invalid_broadcast_fn` error** when this invariant is violated — including when `fn` is absent, for which there is no default; **loading MUST fail**.
clauses.note: Load fails with invalid_broadcast_fn for a broadcast with absent, non-scalar or wrong-arity fn.

clauses.quote: It has no axis to align to, so bindings MUST reject the document with the structural diagnostic `array_shape_mismatch` (Section 7). Both shapes are declared, so this is decidable statically and MUST be decided at validation time
clauses.note: validate rejects with array_shape_mismatch any elementwise operand whose declared index sets are not a subset of the result's.

clauses.quote: The two spellings MUST agree bit for bit.
clauses.note: A bare elementwise array expression over named operands equals, element for element and bitwise, the equivalent full-map faq over the result axes.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST NOT let the value's rank replace the declared shape
clauses.note: An equation giving a shaped variable a scalar RHS assigns that value to every element of the declared shape.

clauses.quote: bindings MUST reject `fn` nodes whose `name` is not in the registry for the file's declared `esm` version. There is no per-file declaration
clauses.note: A fn node naming a function outside the registry for the declared esm version is rejected.

clauses.quote: Bindings MUST emit an `unknown_closed_function` error when this invariant is violated; loading MUST fail.
clauses.note: The rejection of an unregistered fn name carries code unknown_closed_function and fails load.

clauses.quote: `enum_name` MUST match a key in the top-level `enums` block (Section 9.3); `symbol` MUST match a key declared under that enum.
clauses.note: An enum node is well-formed only if its enum name and symbol are declared.

clauses.quote: Bindings MUST reject references to undeclared enums or undeclared symbols within an enum at load time, with diagnostic codes `unknown_enum` and `unknown_enum_symbol` respectively.
clauses.note: An undeclared enum yields unknown_enum and an undeclared symbol yields unknown_enum_symbol at load; a declared pair lowers to its integer const.

clauses.quote: There is **no depth limit**, and a resolver MUST walk every segment
clauses.note: A scoped reference s₁…sₙ resolves by walking s₁ through subsystems maps to sₙ₋₁ and looking up sₙ there, at any depth.

clauses.quote: A binding without remote support MUST reject a URL ref **cleanly** with the existing unresolved diagnostics
clauses.note: Network capability of a binding; the model performs no I/O.

clauses.quote: A binding that does support URLs MUST treat a URL-loaded document as the base for that document's own relative refs
clauses.note: Remote fetching and URL joining are file/network I/O, outside the model.

clauses.quote: Two mount forms that merged different things would make an assembly's meaning depend on which attachment point the author happened to pick; a binding MUST NOT make them differ.
clauses.note: Mounting a component via subsystems.<k> or via top-level models.<k> yields the same resolved component and the same index-set merge; only its landing place differs.

clauses.quote: a binding that does not implement a mount form MUST refuse the entry with `mount_form_unsupported` (§9.6.6) at its pointer
clauses.note: Refusal for a capability a binding lacks; the model implements every mount form.

clauses.quote: It MUST NOT depend on whether the leaf happens to declare `metaparameters`, or to import a template library
clauses.note: An unclosed index-set size in a mounted leaf merges upward symbolically whether or not the leaf declares metaparameters or imports templates.

clauses.quote: is exactly what "a binding MUST NOT make them differ" forbids
clauses.note: Loader-API metaparameter bindings seed a mounted leaf's close, filtered to the names the leaf declares, identically at both mount forms and at every depth.

clauses.quote: a referenced document's own mount edges MUST be resolved, in that document's directory and against that document's own registry, before its single top-level system is extracted and before its `index_sets` merge upward.
clauses.note: Mounting an assembly resolves its own mount edges first, so mounting composes to any depth at both forms.

clauses.quote: Cycle detection MUST be path-scoped — pushed when an edge is entered and popped when it is left — so the same component file may be mounted under several keys, and only a cycle along the current resolution path is an error; the diagnostic MUST name the cycle rather than recursing without bound.
clauses.note: Mount resolution terminates; it errors (naming the cycle) iff a file recurs along one resolution path, and accepts DAG-shaped reuse.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST NOT merge before that close.
clauses.note: The index-set merge folds an incoming contribution against the mounting document's closed metaparameter environment and compares folded forms deep-equal.
clauses.concern: This states normatively that the merge runs after the mounting document's close, yet the 'Two mount forms' paragraph above says Rust and Julia merge before it, Python/TypeScript/Go after, and that 'which side of that merge order is right' is open — the spec both decides and leaves open the same question.

clauses.quote: An enclosing mount edge's `index_set_rename` MUST NOT rename an axis contributed only by a component the LEAF itself mounts
clauses.note: An edge's index_set_rename vocabulary is the axes the referenced document declares or imports itself; naming one that arrived only via a nested mount is subsystem_index_set_rename_unknown_name.

clauses.quote: A key MUST name an index set of the resolved mounted document, else `subsystem_index_set_rename_unknown_name`
clauses.note: An index_set_rename key that is not an index set of the resolved mounted document is rejected with subsystem_index_set_rename_unknown_name.

clauses.quote: Targets MUST be dotted identifiers (§9.7.7 grammar), else `template_import_rename_invalid`
clauses.note: An index_set_rename target outside the dotted-identifier grammar is rejected with template_import_rename_invalid.

clauses.quote: post-rename names MUST be distinct within the edge, else `template_import_rename_collision`
clauses.note: An index_set_rename whose post-rename names collide is rejected with template_import_rename_collision.

clauses.quote: That section's rule that a binding MUST NOT make the two forms differ is what makes silence unacceptable here: a binding that cannot yet APPLY the field at a form MUST REFUSE that edge
clauses.note: Refusal for a capability a binding lacks (subsystem_index_set_rename_unsupported_mount_form); the model applies renames at every form.

clauses.quote: Therefore `from_faq` MUST be resolved against the expression nodes of the **whole document**, not of one model
clauses.note: A derived index set's from_faq resolves against every expression node id in the document; naming none is unknown_faq_node.
clauses.concern: It justifies document scope by 'the §3 field table', but §3 is Metadata; the field table that makes index_sets document-scoped is in §2.

clauses.quote: an expression-node `id` MUST be unique across the document rather than merely within its model
clauses.note: A document in which two expression nodes share an id is rejected at load.
clauses.concern: A duplicate id is called 'a load-time error' but no diagnostic code is given, so the verdict cannot be pinned as a (code, pointer) pair like the others.

clauses.quote: A component that cannot carry the field MUST be refused at load, not evaluated in the mounting document's precision.
clauses.note: Mounting a document whose precision must be written onto a reaction system is rejected at load with element_type_uncarried.

clauses.quote: A subsystem `ref` MUST NOT target a template-library file (`subsystem_ref_is_template_library`), and a template import MUST NOT target a subsystem/component file (`template_import_not_library`).
clauses.note: A subsystem ref to a template library is subsystem_ref_is_template_library; a template import of a component file is template_import_not_library.

clauses.quote: The injected `ref` MUST resolve to a template-library file (`template_import_not_library` otherwise); the subsystem `ref` itself still MUST resolve to a component file.
clauses.note: On a mount edge, an injected template import must name a template library (else template_import_not_library) and the subsystem ref a component file.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST NOT introduce a ninth axis, and MUST NOT map a registry symbol onto an axis the table below does not give it.
clauses.note: A dimension is a rational vector over exactly m, kg, s, mol, K, A, cd, rad, and each registry symbol's dimension is the one the table gives.

clauses.quote: A general-purpose units library MAY be used as the arithmetic engine, but it MUST be constrained to this table and these axes.
clauses.note: Unit resolution agrees with the §4.8.1 table on every symbol, whatever engine computes it.

clauses.quote: A binding whose underlying units library *does* have a prefix mechanism (pint, uom, Unitful) MUST disable it or gate lookups on this table.
clauses.note: A unit symbol resolves iff it is a table key exactly as spelled; prefixed compositions not in the table (kmolec, nppb) are unit_parse_error.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST use the values above.
clauses.note: The scales of ft, mi, lb, hp, gal, inHg, Torr, psi, degF, BTU, cal, kcal and the six mixing ratios are exactly the rationals given (cal = 4.184 J thermochemical, ppt = 1e-12).

clauses.quote: A conforming checker MUST decide every scale agreement (§4.8.3) **exactly**, never by comparing floating-point numbers within a tolerance
clauses.note: Scale agreement is equality of exact scales (rationals times powers of π); the verdict never depends on floating-point arithmetic.

clauses.quote: A binding MAY keep a floating-point scale for NUMERIC unit conversion (loaders, coupling transforms), but that float MUST NOT decide a dimensional verdict.
clauses.note: Every dimensional verdict is a function of exact scales only.

clauses.quote: A document that means short tons MUST write `short_ton`
clauses.note: States author intent; the checkable consequence (no `ton` or `t` symbol) is covered by the registry table.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST use `2.6867e20`.
clauses.note: DU and Dobson have dimension m^-2 and exact scale 2.6867e20.

clauses.quote: A conforming parser MUST resolve exactly the strings this grammar and these token rules derive, and MUST NOT resolve any other string.
clauses.note: A unit string resolves iff it lexes by the token rules and derives from the grammar: whitespace-only, m^+2, m^1e3, s1, a bare degree sign do not resolve; m ^ 2 and %h do.

clauses.quote: The diagnostic MUST say that a number other than 1 is a scaling factor and that a rational exponent is spelled `^(p/q)`.
clauses.note: A unit string with a numeric atom other than 1 is unit_parse_error, and the message names the scaling-factor reason and the ^(p/q) spelling.

clauses.quote: so a lexer MUST admit `%` as a symbol token
clauses.note: "%" and "%/h" lex and resolve (scale 0.01, dimensionless).
clauses.concern: 'A symbol is a maximal run of characters that is a table key' does not say whether a run is delimited by character class (so `s1` is one unresolvable token) or is the longest table-key prefix (so `s1` lexes as `s` followed by the legal atom `1`, i.e. `s*1`, which the grammar's optional-operator juxtaposition accepts); the two readings disagree on strings like `kg1` and `s1`.

clauses.quote: All operands MUST share a dimension **and a scale**; the result is that unit.
clauses.note: The determinable operands of +/− must have equal dimension and exact scale; undeterminable ones are skipped; with none determinable the result is undeterminable.
clauses.concern: The row is headed '`+` `-` (n-ary)' and the constant-expression rule treats `-` over two or more operands as a left fold, but the §4.2 arithmetic table gives `-` arity 'unary or binary'; whether a three-operand `-` is legal is stated both ways.

clauses.quote: The exponent MUST be dimensionless.
clauses.note: A ^ with a dimensional exponent is a mismatch; a constant-expression exponent raises dimension and scale exactly; any other exponent makes the result undeterminable.

clauses.quote: `sqrt` is NOT a transcendental and MUST NOT be given the dimensionless-argument rule
clauses.note: sqrt halves every exponent of its operand's dimension and scale and accepts any dimension.

clauses.quote: The operands whose unit is determinable MUST share a dimension and a scale, and an undeterminable operand is skipped exactly as in `+` `-`
clauses.note: Determinable comparison operands must agree in dimension and scale; the result is dimensionless.

clauses.quote: Its operands follow the `+` rule: every determinable operand MUST share a dimension and a scale
clauses.note: concat's determinable operands must agree; the result is their shared unit or undeterminable.

clauses.quote: Its region `values` follow the `+` rule: determinable values MUST share a dimension and a scale
clauses.note: makearray's determinable region values must agree; the result is their shared unit or undeterminable.

clauses.quote: The argument MUST be a **plane angle** (`rad`, or `deg`, which carries the `rad` dimension to the FIRST power) **or dimensionless at scale 1**. The result is dimensionless. A plane angle is admitted at **any scale**, and an implementation MUST **CONVERT** it to radians before evaluating
clauses.note: sin/cos/tan accept rad^1 at any scale or dimensionless at scale 1 (not sr), and the value is computed on the argument converted to radians.

clauses.quote: The argument MUST be **dimensionless at scale 1**. The result is an **angle** (`rad`).
clauses.note: asin/acos/atan require a dimensionless scale-1 argument and return rad.

clauses.quote: The two operands MUST be **COMMENSURATE with each other** — same dimension and same scale, but ANY dimension, not necessarily dimensionless. The result is an **angle** (`rad`). `atan2` is the ONE inverse-trig op that does not take a dimensionless argument: it takes a *ratio not yet formed*, so `atan2(dy_m, dx_m)` is the ordinary spelling of a bearing and MUST be admitted.
clauses.note: atan2 is accepted iff its operands agree in dimension and scale (any dimension), with result rad.

clauses.quote: The argument MUST be **dimensionless at scale 1** — a PURE NUMBER — and the result is dimensionless. The set is EXACTLY
clauses.note: log, log10, exp, sinh, cosh, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh require a dimensionless scale-1 argument.

clauses.quote: An implementation MUST apply the declared scale to reach radians before evaluating a circular function, in every binding.
clauses.note: Evaluating sin/cos/tan of an argument whose unit (by the §4.8.3 rules, array ops included) is deg multiplies by π/180 first: sin(90 deg) = 1.

clauses.quote: the two units MUST have the same dimension and the same exact scale (§4.8.1)
clauses.note: Every agreement (operands, equation sides, observed vs declared unit) requires equal dimension and equal exact scale.
clauses.concern: The same paragraph refers to 'the ten strict transcendentals', but the §4.8.3 table says the strict set is 'EXACTLY ... nine ops, and no others'.

clauses.quote: a conforming checker **REFUSES** rather than picking one, and the diagnostic MUST name the **repair**, not only the refusal
clauses.note: A transcendental of a dimensionless argument at scale ≠ 1 is unit_dimension_mismatch, and the message names the repair (divide by 1 of that unit).

clauses.quote: A checker MUST NOT silently normalize instead
clauses.note: A dimensionless-but-scaled argument to a strict transcendental is rejected, never rescaled.

clauses.quote: **An undeterminable dimension MUST NOT be reported as dimensionless.**
clauses.note: An op with no rule, or a rule with nothing to read, yields 'unknown' (skip), never dimensionless; no false mismatch arises from such an op.

clauses.quote: **An incomplete registry MUST NOT be papered over by downgrading the severity.**
clauses.note: A unit string that does not parse or names a non-registry symbol is always the hard error unit_parse_error, never a warning or dimensionless.

clauses.quote: Name Resolution: what a checker MUST NOT call undefined `undefined_variable`, `undefined_parameter`, `event_var_undeclared` and `unresolved_scoped_ref` are hard errors, so every symbol this section declares to be **in scope** is a symbol a checker MUST resolve.
clauses.note: No symbol that §4.9 declares in scope is reported as undefined_variable, undefined_parameter, event_var_undeclared or unresolved_scoped_ref.

clauses.quote: A checker MUST NOT emit `event_var_undeclared` for `_var` in a model that is operator-composed or that is a coupling target.
clauses.note: _var in an operator-composed or coupling-target model never yields event_var_undeclared.

clauses.quote: A DECLARATION MUST NOT spell one of them (`reserved_variable_name`)
clauses.note: A key in models.variables, an inline subsystem's variables, or a reaction system's species/parameters equal to domain.independent_variable (default t) or _var is rejected with reserved_variable_name at that key.

clauses.quote: so its `variables` map is a declaration map like any other and a checker MUST recurse into every inline subsystem
clauses.note: The reserved-name check applies to inline subsystems at every depth (including spliced-in mounts).

clauses.quote: A declared name MUST NOT contain a control character A key of a declaration map MUST NOT contain a NUL or any other C0 control character (U+0000–U+001F) or DEL (U+007F).
clauses.note: A declaration-map key containing U+0000–U+001F or U+007F fails schema validation at load.

clauses.quote: A resolver MUST **walk** the path — take the last segment as the name and resolve the preceding segments one at a time against each parent's `subsystems` map. A resolver MUST NOT split on `"."` and treat segment `[0]` as the system and segment `[1]` as the variable.
clauses.note: Resolution of an n-segment reference (n ≥ 2), including a coupling system path, walks subsystems; it never treats segments 2..n as one name.

clauses.quote: `initialization_equations` (§6.2) are a *separate* block with a separate balance and MUST NOT be counted into the main one.
clauses.note: The equation_count_mismatch balance counts unknowns against main equations of every LHS form, excluding initialization_equations.

clauses.quote: A checker MUST resolve the free symbols of **every** Expression in the document, wherever it appears
clauses.note: An undefined name in any expression-bearing field of the table is reported with that row's code and pointer.

clauses.quote: a forcing field delivered by the host at runtime MUST still be declared
clauses.note: There are no implicitly-declared host forcings: an undeclared name outside §4.9.1 and the listed declaration sites is undefined.

clauses.quote: **And within an Expression, the walk MUST descend every child field, not just `args`.**
clauses.note: Free-symbol resolution descends args and expr, filter, key, lower, upper, values, axes and bindings.

clauses.quote: An evaluator MUST NOT produce a value for a name bound in none of the scopes available where it evaluates; it MUST fail closed, naming the name.
clauses.note: Evaluating an expression with a free name unbound in the environment is an error naming that name, never a value.
clauses.concern: The supporting claim that 'IEEE-754 max and min return the non-NaN operand' is not true in general: IEEE 754-2019 `maximum`/`minimum` propagate NaN (only `maximumNumber`/`minimumNumber`, and 2008's maxNum, return the number), and of the binding languages Julia `max`, JS `Math.max`, Go `math.Max` and NumPy `maximum` propagate NaN while Rust `f64::max` and C `fmax` do not.

clauses.quote: the check MUST be one shared implementation every route invokes
clauses.note: Code-structure requirement on a binding.

clauses.quote: Every binding MUST reject it, with diagnostic `observed_cycle`, and the diagnostic MUST **name the observeds on the cycle**.
clauses.note: A model whose observed dependency graph (minus recurrence-candidate self-edges) has a cycle is rejected with observed_cycle, naming a cycle.

clauses.quote: it MUST NOT rely on the build to be the only place this is caught
clauses.note: validate alone, without building, rejects an observed cycle.

clauses.quote: The traversal MUST be deterministic — sorted roots, sorted successors — so a binding names the same cycle on every run
clauses.note: details.cycle is the cycle found by depth-first search from sorted roots over sorted successors, closed by repeating its entry node.
clauses.concern: 'Sorted' names no order (code point, UTF-8 bytes, locale), and which cycle and rotation a DFS reports depends on unstated details (whether it stops at the first back edge, which node it enters on), so two compliant bindings can report different `details.cycle` paths.

clauses.quote: Every `lhs` MUST name an **unknown**; an event that writes a parameter is `event_affects_parameter`.
clauses.note: A discrete event affect whose lhs names a parameter is rejected with event_affects_parameter.

clauses.quote: **A single rule MUST be the object form.** A one-element array is invalid
clauses.note: An update given as a one-element array is rejected; arrays have length ≥ 2.

clauses.quote: This is why a `schedule`, `data`, or `remesh` parameter MUST declare its `shape`
clauses.note: A parameter with any update rule of kind schedule, data or remesh and no shape is rejected.
